index_title: Point-generated canonical unary SAP and off-closure coordinate orbits
scope: Private B043: ONE selected Foundations I result and its PGO equation, six definitions, 26 human claims and four tasks. The category consists of finite COMPLETE INDUCED POINT-GENERATED objects over full point-generated bases in an ACTUAL canonical unary interpreted expansion of the homogeneous real source. It is not the hereditary category allowing orphan hidden bases. Old real homogeneity and equivariance replace any assumption that the whole hidden structure is homogeneous. No CCO, symmetry, exact multiplication, countability or new external published provider is required.
scope_explanation: Keep the real source and actual interpreted expansion, full induced embeddings, one-source unary term values including identities, and full point-generated bases visible throughout. Separate this category from arbitrary closed hidden bases.

assumptions.name: Actual homogeneous real source
assumptions.statement: M is a homogeneous complete structure on its ORIGINAL named real sorts; homogeneity means every finite induced original partial isomorphism extends to FULL Aut(M). The interpreted expansion retains these real sorts with their full original induced structure and sort-preserving embeddings. No cardinality/countability, CCO, symmetry or exact-domain premise is assumed.

assumptions.name: Actual canonical unary interpretation
assumptions.statement: Mhat is an ACTUAL canonical equivariant interpreted expansion of M. Every g in Aut(M) induces an automorphism of Mhat which commutes with the named typed unary coordinate maps. All hidden relations are canonical interpretations in M and embeddings of the actual induced objects preserve and reflect them. Every expanded vertex is a named well-sorted unary-term value of some real point, with identity terms retaining real generators.

assumptions.name: Finite full closures without nullary generators
assumptions.statement: For every finite real D, Dhat is its FULL closure under all named typed unary maps and finite compositions, INCLUDING identity terms, and is finite. There are no additional nullary generators or maps with two or more inputs. Relation symbols do not create generated vertices.

assumptions.name: Actual induced point-generated category
assumptions.statement: Objects are finite COMPLETE INDUCED substructures of Mhat generated by finite real sets, or induced-isomorphic copies thereof; arrows are sort-preserving induced embeddings preserving all named maps and the complete real reduct. Every target therefore embeds into actual Mhat by definition. Bases in SAP are FULL point-generated objects, including empty. No SAP over arbitrary orphan closed bases is asserted.

imports.name: Abstract simultaneous finite-action avoidance
imports.statement: For ANY group action, finite moving set S with every orbit infinite, and finite forbidden Z, there is ONE g sending ALL S outside Z. Reuse ONLY the elementary coset-cover proof; empty S/Z and nonfaithful actions are allowed. No topology, CCO, real closure, owner geometry or EPPA premise is imported.
imports.provider_support_usage: C01 proves the abstract virtual-containment preorder and C02 proves the finite coset-cover lemma; they are strict proved ancestors of C03, which converts forbidden action incidences into transporter cosets and yields simultaneous avoidance. Extract their abstract group/action hypotheses only, never CCO/owner branches.

definitions.name: Full point-generated unary closure
definitions.statement: Dhat=union over x in D of all well-sorted named unary-term values of x, including x itself. With no nullary generators, emptyhat is empty and (P union Q)hat=Phat union Qhat.

definitions.name: Induced real generator map
definitions.statement: An induced embedding of a point-generated object restricts to an induced embedding of its real generators. Its value on each tau(x) is forced to be tau(image(x)). This determines its entire map and permits a real homogeneity alignment to align every base coordinate.

definitions.name: Original real-base action
definitions.statement: G_D=FULL Aut(M/D) acts on the actual disjoint expanded carrier via the canonical interpretation. For every u its orbit uses this SAME action; it is not silently replaced by Aut(Mhat/Dhat) or an unrelated subgroup.

definitions.name: PGO condition
definitions.statement: For every finite REAL D and every expanded u outside Dhat, the actual G_D orbit of u is infinite. Term values in Dhat are fixed. PGO is the conditional antecedent in the forward implication, not assumed when proving it from SAP.

definitions.name: Point-generated strong amalgam
definitions.statement: For any induced span Dhat to P1hat,P2hat, a point-generated target and induced leg embeddings form a strong amalgam when their images meet EXACTLY in the displayed base image. Relations between opposite legs are induced from an actual host; no free relational amalgam is requested.

definitions.name: Repeated strong copies over one base
definitions.statement: Iterate binary point-generated SAP to produce n induced copies of a finite point-generated P over ONE fixed full Dhat in a finite point-generated target, with every pair of copies intersecting only in the common base. Later embeddings preserve all earlier distinctness.

claims.name: Unary generation commutes with unions
claims.statement: Every term has one real source, so closure of a finite real union is the union of its individual full closures. Conversely each original closure is included by monotonicity. There are no mixed-input values.

claims.name: Identity terms and the empty closure
claims.statement: Identity terms retain all real generators; no nullary generators gives emptyhat=empty. For a vertex u in any sort, choose a real x and unary term tau with tau(x)=u, using an identity term when u itself is real.

claims.name: The real pointwise stabilizer fixes its entire full closure
claims.statement: If g fixes real D, equivariance implies g tau(d)=tau(gd)=tau(d) for all d in D and terms tau. Hence G_D fixes Dhat pointwise. No hidden homogeneity is used.

claims.name: Real source homogeneity aligns the full interpreted base
claims.statement: Embed both span factors into actual Mhat. Their base maps restrict to an isomorphism of the finite complete real base images. Extend it by original M homogeneity; equivariance and the fact that every base point is a unary term on a real generator make the resulting whole base maps agree.

claims.name: After alignment the common base is a literal point-generated closure
claims.statement: The factors may now be written as actual P1hat and P2hat containing the SAME actual Dhat. They may intersect further before avoidance; no strongness has been presumed at this step.

claims.name: Every off-base point of the moving factor has an infinite orbit under PGO
claims.statement: CONDITIONAL on PGO, the finite moving set S=P2hat minus Dhat consists only of vertices outside Dhat, so every G_D orbit of a point of S is infinite. Z=P1hat is finite by A03.

claims.name: One common stabilizer automorphism separates all extra coordinates
claims.statement: Apply I01 once to the G_D action with moving S and forbidden Z. It produces ONE g in G_D such that g(S) meets P1hat nowhere. Empty moving or forbidden sets are permitted. Independent moves for individual vertices would not suffice.

claims.name: The factor intersection is exactly the common full base
claims.statement: C03 says g fixes Dhat, so Dhat is contained in P1hat intersect gP2hat. Any point of the intersection outside Dhat would belong to g(S) intersect P1hat, contradicting C07. Thus equality holds.

claims.name: The induced union is again a finite point-generated object
claims.statement: Choose finite real generating sets P1 and P2 for the two actual factors. Their moved real union P1 union gP2 is finite, and C01 gives its full closure P1hat union gP2hat. Equip that carrier with ALL relations/functions induced from actual Mhat; it is an object of A04.

claims.name: Both inclusions into the induced union are induced embeddings
claims.statement: Each original factor was an actual complete induced substructure and g is an actual expansion automorphism. The induced union reflects as well as preserves each factor relation and map. Cross-leg relations are inherited from Mhat; no freedom claim is made.

claims.name: PGO implies point-generated SAP
claims.statement: The target in C09 with leg inclusions C10 and exact intersection C08 is a finite point-generated strong amalgam of the arbitrary span. The empty base is allowed by C02; this establishes the forward implication without old SAP or whole-hidden homogeneity.

claims.name: A finite off-closure orbit has positive finite size
claims.statement: For the converse assume ONLY point-generated SAP and suppose some u outside Dhat has finite G_D orbit. Write k=|G_D.u|. Since identity sends u to itself, k>=1. The contradiction will require k+1, not k, distinct copies.

claims.name: One real source packages the offending coordinate into a finite object
claims.statement: Use C02 to choose real x and tau with tau(x)=u, and take Phat=closure(D union {x}). It is finite by A03 and contains u and full Dhat as induced subobjects. Necessarily x is not in D, since otherwise u would lie in Dhat.

claims.name: Iterated SAP makes arbitrarily many copies over the SAME base
claims.statement: Start with one Phat. Given a target containing n copies over Dhat, apply SAP to that target and one fresh Phat over the very same full Dhat. The two target images intersect exactly in Dhat; old factor maps stay injective, preserving all previous intersections. Induction constructs n+1 copies.

claims.name: The k+1 copied offending coordinates are pairwise distinct
claims.statement: Apply C14 with n=k+1. Each copy u_j lies outside the common base because induced leg embeddings are injective and original u is outside Dhat. Distinct copies intersect only in Dhat, hence u_i differs from u_j for i not equal j.

claims.name: The finite target embeds in the actual interpreted structure
claims.statement: The iterated SAP target is an object of the ACTUAL point-generated category A04, hence has an induced embedding into Mhat. This is by category membership, not an assumed hidden Fraisse limit or hidden homogeneity theorem. Distinct copied coordinates remain distinct.

claims.name: Original homogeneity aligns the embedded real base with literal D
claims.statement: Restrict the target embedding on its common base to the induced real D copy. Its inverse partial isomorphism to actual D extends to an original automorphism by A01. Apply its canonical expansion action; equivariance then aligns ALL of the common Dhat, preserving distinctness.

claims.name: Each copied real generator has the same complete real type over D
claims.statement: Let x_j be the real generator image in the aligned jth Phat-copy. The induced leg embedding restricts to an induced original isomorphism D union {x} to D union {x_j}, fixing D and preserving sort and every original relation. Completeness makes this the required complete original finite one-point diagram.

claims.name: Original homogeneity supplies original stabilizer automorphisms
claims.statement: Extend the finite original isomorphism in C18 to g_j in FULL Aut(M). It fixes D pointwise and sends x to x_j, so g_j belongs to exactly the G_D used to define k, without needing to extend a hidden partial isomorphism.

claims.name: All copied coordinates belong to the same original orbit
claims.statement: Named-term preservation gives u_j=tau(x_j); equivariance gives tau(g_j x)=g_j tau(x). Consequently u_j=g_j u. Distinct u_j therefore provide k+1 elements of the k-element actual G_D orbit, a contradiction.

claims.name: Point-generated SAP implies PGO
claims.statement: The contradiction in C20 rules out every finite off-closure orbit for every finite real D. Thus every such orbit is infinite, including D empty. This direction has not used I01 or assumed PGO.

claims.name: Selected source theorem and PGO equation
claims.statement: C11 and C21 prove point-generated SAP over FULL point-generated common bases iff PGO. The real-base original action remains fixed throughout; no hidden-base hereditary SAP statement has been substituted.

claims.name: A named bijection with unnamed inverse separates the two categories
claims.statement: Let M be a countably infinite pure real set, H an interpreted disjoint copy, and f:R->H the named bijection, with no named inverse. Full point-generated closures are D union f(D). Outside such a closure, original permutations fixing D give infinite real and hidden orbits. Thus PGO and point-generated SAP hold. But hereditary closed base {h} with two factors {r,h}, f(r)=h, has no strong amalgam: injectivity of f forces the two real copies equal. The base {h} is NOT point-generated.

claims.name: The unary requirement excludes mixed-generator values
claims.statement: With a genuinely binary generating map, closure(P1 union P2) may contain f(x,y) for x from the first factor and y from the second, absent from both factor closures. The equality used in C09 then fails. No extension of this proof to arbitrary functional arities is claimed.

claims.name: No cardinality or unrelated structural hypothesis is imported
claims.statement: The proof uses finite closures and finite induced real partial isomorphism extension only. It uses no countability, topology, faithfulness of the abstract avoidance action, CCO, symmetry, exact multiplication, global hidden homogeneity or arbitrary hidden-base algebraicity theorem. The sole finite-action import has already expanded abstract group support.

claims.name: Nullary generators and noncanonical expansions require separate contracts
claims.statement: No nullary generators gives the actual empty point-generated base used here. Canonical equivariance and retained complete real reduct justify extending old automorphisms to the expanded carrier and aligning induced base maps. Removing those premises does not leave a proved SAP criterion; no independent arbitrary hidden relation or extra unrepresented coordinate is allowed. The empty-base quantifier is essential: a named unary map from an infinite pure real set to one hidden singleton has infinite off-closure orbits over all NONEMPTY real bases, but its fixed hidden singleton lies outside emptyhat and obstructs SAP over the empty base.

overview_notes: Only the point-generated full-base category is in scope; the named-bijection example separates hereditary SAP.
Forward uses finite avoidance; reverse uses no avoidance or PGO hypothesis.
Identity terms retain real generators and original induced homogeneity supplies all automorphisms.

controls.check: Bounded named-bijection closures, all small point-generated base spans, induced injections, exact intersections and hereditary orphan-base obstruction.
Bounded repeated-copy distinctness and pigeonhole orbit counts, typed unary union/equivariance and a mixed binary generator boundary; no infinite orbit or general SAP theorem certified.

article_feedback.finding: The real source sorts and their complete original induced structure are retained in the interpreted expansion; identity terms retain real generators. Thus an induced base embedding restricts to an original real partial isomorphism and real homogeneity aligns the entire unary-generated base.
